In [[number theory]], '''Vantieghem's theorem''' is a [[primality]] criterion. It states that a [[natural number]] ''n''≥3 is [[prime number|prime]] if and only if
:<math>  \prod_{1 \leq k \leq n-1} \left( 2^k - 1  \right) \equiv n \mod \left(  2^n - 1 \right). </math>

Similarly, ''n'' is prime, if and only if the following [[Modular arithmetic|congruence]] for [[polynomial]]s in ''X'' holds:
:<math>  \prod_{1 \leq k \leq n-1} \left( X^k - 1  \right) \equiv  n- \left( X^n - 1 \right)/\left( X - 1 \right) \mod \left(  X^n - 1 \right) </math>

or:
:<math>  \prod_{1 \leq k \leq n-1} \left( X^k - 1  \right) \equiv n \mod \left( X^n - 1 \right)/\left( X - 1 \right). </math>

== Example ==
Let n=7 forming the product 1*3*7*15*31*63 = 615195.  615195 = 7 mod 127 and so 7 is prime<br>
Let n=9 forming the product 1*3*7*15*31*63*127*255 = 19923090075.  19923090075 = 301 mod 511  and so 9 is composite
